Viesintos Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Utena County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Viesintos's Jews enjoyed notably warm relations with the local landowning Komar family — when the community began building its Beit Midrash in the summer of 1879, General Constantin Komar personally supported and encouraged the effort and gave them the land for this cemetery; when he later died, many of the town's Jews attended his funeral. A yeshiva was built in the town in 1911, and a Shas society studied Judaic texts there. At the end of September 1941, Viesintos's Jews were taken to Kupiskis, documented elsewhere in this collection, and murdered alongside that town's own Jewish community in a common mass grave.
